pairs: Melior est buccella sicca cum gaudio quam domus plena victimis cum jurgio.
A dry morsel with gladness is better than a house full of sacrifices along with conflict.
Servus sapiens dominabitur filiis stultis,
A wise servant shall rule over foolish sons,
et inter fratres hæreditatem dividet.
and he will divide the inheritance among brothers.
Sicut igne probatur argentum
Just as silver is tested by fire,
et aurum camino,
and gold is tested in the furnace,
ita corda probat Dominus.
so also does the Lord test hearts.
Malus obedit linguæ iniquæ,
The evil obey an unjust tongue.
et fallax obtemperat labiis mendacibus.
And the false are submissive to lying lips.
Qui despicit pauperem exprobrat factori ejus,
Whoever despises the poor rebukes his Maker.
et qui ruina lætatur alterius non erit impunitus.
And whoever rejoices in the ruin of another will not go unpunished.
Corona senum filii filiorum,
Sons of sons are the crown of old age.
et gloria filiorum patres eorum.
And the glory of sons is their fathers.
Non decent stultum verba composita,
Well-chosen words are not fitting for the foolish,
nec principem labium mentiens.
nor are lying lips fitting for a leader.
Gemma gratissima exspectatio præstolantis;
The expectation of those who stand ready is a most pleasing jewel.
quocumque se vertit,
Whichever way he turns himself,
prudenter intelligit.
he understands prudently.
Qui celat delictum quærit amicitias;
Whoever conceals an offense seeks friendships.
qui altero sermone repetit, separat fœderatos.
Whoever repeats the words of another separates allies.
Plus proficit correptio apud prudentem,
A correction benefits more with a wise man,
quam centum plagæ apud stultum.
than a hundred stripes with a fool.
Semper jurgia quærit malus:
The evil one continually seeks conflicts.
angelus autem crudelis mittetur contra eum.
But a cruel Angel shall be sent against him.
Expedit magis ursæ occurrere raptis fœtibus,
It is more expedient to meet a bear robbed of her young,
quam fatuo confidenti in stultitia sua.
than the foolish trusting in his own folly.
Qui reddit mala pro bonis,
Whoever repays evil for good,
non recedet malum de domo ejus.
evil shall not withdraw from his house.
Qui dimittit aquam caput est jurgiorum,
Whoever releases the water is the head of the conflict.
et antequam patiatur contumeliam judicium deserit.
And just before he suffers contempt, he abandons judgment.
Qui justificat impium,
Those who justify the impious,
et qui condemnat justum,
and those who condemn the just,
abominabilis est uterque apud Deum.
both are abominable with God.
Quid prodest stulto habere divitias,
What does it profit the foolish to have riches,
cum sapientiam emere non possit?
when he is not able to buy wisdom?
Qui altum facit domum suam quærit ruinam,
Whoever makes his house high seeks ruin.
et qui evitat discere incidet in mala.
And whoever shuns learning shall fall into evils.
Omni tempore diligit qui amicus est,
Whoever is a friend loves at all times.
et frater in angustiis comprobatur.
And a brother is proved by distress.
Stultus homo plaudet manibus,
A foolish man will clap his hands,
cum spoponderit pro amico suo.
when he makes a pledge for his friend.
Qui meditatur discordias diligit rixas,
Whoever dwells on discord loves disputes.
et qui exaltat ostium quærit ruinam.
And whoever exalts his door seeks ruin.
Qui perversi cordis est non inveniet bonum,
Whoever is of a perverse heart shall not find good.
et qui vertit linguam incidet in malum.
And whoever turns his tongue shall fall into evil.
Natus est stultus in ignominiam suam;
A foolish one is born into his own disgrace.
sed nec pater in fatuo lætabitur.
But his father will not rejoice in one who is senseless.
Animus gaudens ætatem floridam facit;
A joyful soul makes a lifetime flourish.
spiritus tristis exsiccat ossa.
A gloomy spirit dries out the bones.
Munera de sinu impius accipit,
The impious receives gifts from the bosom,
ut pervertat semitas judicii.
so that he may pervert the paths of judgment.
In facie prudentis lucet sapientia;
Prudence shines from the face of the wise.
oculi stultorum in finibus terræ.
The eyes of the foolish are on the ends of the earth.
Ira patris filius stultus,
A foolish son is the anger of the father
et dolor matris quæ genuit eum.
and the grief of the mother who conceived him.
Non est bonum damnum inferre justo,
It is not good to inflict damage on the just,
nec percutere principem qui recta judicat.
nor to strike the leader who judges uprightly.
Qui moderatur sermones suos doctus et prudens est,
Whoever moderates his words is learned and prudent.
et pretiosi spiritus vir eruditus.
And a man of learning has a precious spirit.
Stultus quoque, si tacuerit,
If he would remain silent,
sapiens reputabitur, et si compresserit labia sua,
even the foolish would be considered wise, and if he closes his lips,
intelligens.
intelligent.
